title: He was breathing hard.
paragraphs:
He was breathing hard.
Grip tight.
Blade ready.
And one whisper changed everything.
“Let me strike him… just once.” (1 Samuel 26:8)
That was Abishai—loyal, fearless, dangerous.
And honestly?
He wasn’t wrong… at least not in human logic.
Because right there, in the dead of night, lay Saul—the man hunting David like an animal.

Sleeping.
Defenseless.
Delivered.

No guards waking.
No resistance rising.
No consequence—at least on the surface.
This was the moment every wounded heart dreams about.

The moment where pain meets power.
Where injustice meets opportunity.
Where revenge finally feels… righteous.
And Abishai stepped forward.

Sword in hand.
Fire in his chest.
Justice in his eyes.
“God has given him into your hand.”
Careful.
Because not every “God moment” is from God.
Some are just your anger… wearing Scripture as a mask.
Pause there.
Let that hit.

Abishai wasn’t a villain.
He was a warrior.
A protector.
A man who loved David enough to kill for him.
But love without submission becomes destruction.

Because he was ready to do something that sounded spiritual…
but violated something sacred.
And then—David speaks.
“Do not destroy him… who can stretch out his hand against the Lord’s anointed and be guiltless?” (1 Samuel 26:9)
Silence.
Tension.
A blade frozen mid-air.
David saw what Abishai couldn’t:
You don’t fulfill God’s promise by breaking God’s command.
Let’s bring it closer.
Some of you right now…
You have the spear.
Not a literal one—but don’t lie, you feel it.

The text message you could send.
The secret you could expose.
The reputation you could destroy.
The clapback you’ve been rehearsing in your head.
And it feels justified.

They hurt you.
They lied.
They betrayed.
They made you bleed.
So now you want balance.

But heaven is not asking for balance.
Heaven is asking for surrender.

Because vengeance feels powerful…
until it poisons you.
Abishai thought he was ending a problem.
But David knew—he would be starting a consequence.
And this is where the story flips.
Not with a kill.
But with restraint.
David doesn’t take Saul’s life.
He takes Saul’s spear… and his water jug. (1 Samuel 26:11–12)
Why?
Because sometimes God will let you get close enough to prove your heart…
but not to act on your impulse.
That proximity is a test.
Will you obey when it costs you your release?
Will you trust when delay feels like injustice?
Will you honor God… when it would be easier to win without Him?
And here is where the Gospel explodes into the story.

Because this isn’t just about Abishai.
This isn’t just about David.
This is about you.
And me.
Because deep down, we’ve all been Abishai.

We’ve all held the weapon.
We’ve all justified the strike.
We’ve all mistaken emotion for righteousness.
But look at Jesus.
The greater David.
When He stood before His enemies—He had more than a spear.

He had authority.
Legions of angels.
The power to end it all in a breath.
And yet…
He didn’t strike.
He stretched out His hands.

Nailed.
Pierced.
Bleeding.
Not because He was weak.
But because He chose mercy over vengeance.
“Father, forgive them…” (Luke 23:34)
That is power.
Real power.
Not the ability to destroy your enemies…
but the authority to forgive them.
So now the question is not:
“Do you have the chance to strike?”
The real question is:
Do you have the courage to obey?

Because obedience will cost you your pride.
It will cost you your timing.
It will cost you the satisfaction of being right—right now.
But it will save your soul from becoming what hurt you.
Listen—
God does not need your sin to fulfill His promise.
He doesn’t need your revenge to defend your calling.
He doesn’t need your anger to establish your future.
If He said it—He will do it.
Without your disobedience.
So breathe.
Lower the weapon.
Step back from that edge.
Let God be God.
And let grace interrupt your instinct.
Because one day, you will stand where Saul stood—
in need of mercy you did not deserve.
And the only reason you will receive it…
is because Jesus chose the cross over the spear.
Repent.
Release it.
Return to Him.
Lay down what your flesh is gripping so tightly.
Pick up what your Savior already carried.
“Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.” (Romans 12:21)
This is your moment.
Not to win.
But to obey.
Not to strike.
But to surrender.
Not to prove a point…
but to reflect a King.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
